findings.title: matchedEntryStepId WARN logs triggerType (low-cardinality category, not a value) — acceptable but confirm classification
findings.description: LOG_DISPATCH_NO_MATCHED_ELEMENT logs `funnelId={} triggerType={}`. triggerType is a fixed taxonomy value ('event'/'keyword'/'tag_added'/'custom_field_set') chosen by the funnel author at design time, NOT the runtime triggerValue/matchKey/event_name. It is a code/category, so it complies with Decision 16 (ids/codes only, never event_name/triggerValue). Flagged only so a reviewer explicitly confirms triggerType is treated as a code and not later widened to include matchKey. No PII or business-secret leakage in any of the new LOG_* statements (LOG_DISPATCH_REDIRECT, LOG_DISPATCH_FUNNEL_ERROR, LOG_REDIRECT, LOG_REDIRECT_CLAIM_LOST, LOG_REDIRECT_BROKEN_CURSOR all carry ids/codes only; LOG_DISPATCH_FUNNEL_ERROR logs exception simpleName, not message).
findings.impact: None as written. If triggerType were ever replaced with matchKey/triggerValue it would leak business-event names to logs (Decision 16 violation).
findings.recommendation: Keep triggerType (category) in the WARN; never substitute matchKey/triggerValue. Current code is correct.

findings.title: Redirect decision relies on two non-atomic steps (in-flight probe then CAS) — defense-in-depth holds, but document the TOCTOU window
findings.description: inFlightExecutionId() does a findOne, then redirectExecution() does a separate findAndModify CAS. Between the probe and the CAS the row could change (sweep claims it, or status transitions). This is NOT an IDOR/security defect because: (1) the executionId is sourced ONLY from the trusted project+funnel+subscriber-scoped probe, never from request input; (2) claimForRedirect re-checks _id AND subscriberId AND funnelId AND status-in(running,waiting,waiting_for_reply) AND stepRunStatus=pending atomically, so a stale id, a sweep-owned row, or a mismatched subscriber/funnel deterministically loses the CAS and becomes a no-op + WARN (no retry, Decision 4). The TOCTOU window is therefore benign (worst case: a redirect that the dispatcher believed would happen becomes a logged no-op). Raised only as a correctness/observability note, not a vulnerability.
findings.impact: No security impact. At most an occasional no-op redirect under concurrency, already covered by LOG_REDIRECT_CLAIM_LOST.
findings.recommendation: No change required. The atomic CAS is the authoritative anti-IDOR gate; the probe is only an optimization/id-source. Behavior is already asserted by redirect_casLost_isNoOp_andEmitsWarn.
